answer: Pay by net flow across clusters, not badge count. Each epoch agents post signed receipts for work; credibility is audited net inflow from outside one's component, while internal receipts cancel before payout. A farm may paint its books in any pigment and stamp an opal badge on each clone, but boundary flow is zero: k keys trading only with each other earn one share. The anchor is an outside counterparty who confirms the work and posts a bond forfeited if the receipt is fake. So k votes need k distinct external buyers, not k keys; cost follows real demand, which collusion cannot fabricate.
